x: For those who are are not 'au fait' with the team,the regular members are:- Jim Vivian,Chris Martin,Denis Gleeson and Clive Oliver. Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major.

Chris Martin put up a couple of really good times in the sprints, winning the 220y and placing 2nd in the 100y. In the quarter mile Philip Smith recorded a personal best and with a little more experience should improve this time even further.
In the absence of Jim Vivian (just out of hospital after an appendicitis operation) the Belgrave flag was still kept flying in the sprints with good efforts by Chris Martin and Denis Gleeson.
One of the mainstays of our Junior section is Chris Martin,who as usual took both sprints in good times. He is consistently around 23 secs for the longer race and is an athlete of great potential.

In the 220 yards Chris Martin was closer to the winner in the final than the times suggest,running very strongly to record 22.8. The combination of these two plus Gleeson and Oliver was far too strong for any other team the South of England could put up.
Ben Lulham's 'stable' was well to the forefront in the absence of Jim Vivian (appendicitis) both 100y and 220y were won by Chris Martin with Denis Gleeson and C.Oliver second and third in both races.
With brilliant baton passing, Denis Gleeson and Chris Martin put us even further ahead and when Jim Vivian took the baton for the last leg it was all over.
September 15th - Hornchurch JUNIOR INTER-COUNTY CHRIS MARTIN SETS TWO PERSONAL BESTS Team:- 1.Surrey 143pts 2.Essex 141pts 3.Kent 81pts
4 x 110 yards · J.Mitchell,D.Gleeson, C.Martin, J.Vivian . · Sept.1965 · 42.8 secs.
The very gusty weather spoilt some of the times but Chris Martin's furlong looked very strong, although he later expressed disappointment at it being so slow.

We did not expect too much of our sprint relay team but one thing that did stand out was the running of Chris Martin. On the last leg he brought the team up into 4th place and it looks as if we shall see great things from him this season.
Chris Martin improved on his best furlong time this year with a 22.9 and Denis Gleeson, running his first 'quarter' of the season, returned a promising 53.1 .
Chris Martin and Philip Gee showed some good form in the sprints and Pete Pepe in his first race of the year clocked a good 16.4 for the high hurdles, finishing 3rd.

Chris Martin clocked 22.7 in the furlong heats finishing 2nd to Mel Cheskin(Poly H) 21.9.These were the two fastest times of the day. Qualifiers for finals:- 220y:C.Martin 22.7, 3miles:Gerry North 14:21.2 A.Major 14:19.2

A great display of sprinting was put up by Chris Martin, our only Senior sprinter in the Championships, the climax coming when he chased the international Mel Cheskin (Poly) home in the final of the 220yds.
Poly had three internationals in Campbell, Frith and Cheskin - LAC had Winbolt-Lewis and Marsh - and running in "claret and gold" were John Mitchell and Chris Martin.

Chris Martin in the "B" race had no trouble in disposing of John Marsh (LAC). Adrian Major, now enjoying track running even more than cross-country, gave a great display of uninhibited running, leading past the bell in the 880yds in 57.0 .but unfortunately slipping back during the 2nd lap.

Derek Wade held 2nd place for most of the competition until John Mitchell, unable to produce his best form, displaced him with a 22 footer. Chris Martin started a busy couple of hours by chasing home John in the 100yds, later reversing the result in the furlong.
Does Chris Martin ever have an off day ? Once again he treated us to a win in his speciality the furlong, chased home by John Mitchell who had earlier taken the 100 yds.
In the sprints Chris Martin ran only one-tenth slower than his best in the final of the furlong, won by Steane (TVH) with 21.5, and also finished 4th in the heats of the 100yds in 10.4 .
The best performances in this light hearted match against our local rivals came from Chris Martin in the 'quarter' and Anthony Heath in the mile.
(Photo:E.D.Lacey)Belgrave Harriers 4X220 Relay Team. l.to r. J.Vivian, C.Martin,R.Nelson,J.Mitchell.
After the number of club trustees had been promptly reduced from five to four, honours badges were presented to: Seniors - C.Martin, C.Clair and J.Bicourt

The main stay of our sprinters is Chris Martin, scorer of more points in our Club matches than any other person. In the Surrey County 4 x 110y and 4 x 440y our 2nd and 3rd places were due mainly to him, although there was some good backing from other members especially from Terry Derham in the shorter race.
We were well represented in the sprints, John Mitchell finishing extremely close to Jim Vivian in the 100y and Chris Martin grabbing 3rd in the furlong.
Lacey)---Chris Martin trails the majestic Winbolt-Lewis in a heat of the Surrey Co 220yds. Both qualified for the final, run four days later, in which Vivian was 2nd and Martin 4th.
Vivian again outpaced the Cambridge men for an even time furlong with this time Chris Martin providing the backing with another win in the 'B' race.

Tony Brooks gave us a good lead on the first leg which was steadily improved upon by John Mitchell, Chris Martin and Jim Vivian and we finished streets ahead in our race but 3rd overall in 3:24.5 our best time for ages.

…d these events, but now that John Mitchell has had an unlucky start to the season due to glandular fever Jim Vivian and Chris Martin had both better look out for the fast improving Steve White, who has recorded times over the longer sprint that Jim and Chris have yet to beat this year.…

The outstanding performers at this year's championships were Steve White, Chris Martin and Nick Head. The first two chalked up sprint trebles in the Junior & Senior grades respectively, and the latter repeated his "pinta" treble of last year shot/discus/javelin.

In the Senior sprints Jim Vivian resumed his duels with Tymms (Surrey AC) and had Chris Martin to keep him company in both finals. Jim could not reproduce the excellent start he gained in his 100 heat and trailed Tymms throughout by a frustrating yard.

This defeat can mainly be blamed on Hillingdon's Andy Kerr who trains with Bels. Full marks to Chris Martin who scored a double in the sprints, Adrian Major for a personal best mile and Bill Kerr in the three miles.

Chris Martin did both sprints and both of the relays. Adrian Major ran the mile and 3 miles, Tony Brooks the half mile,triple jump and both relays, Denzil Winsborrow 3 events and Bob Couillault 3 events.

Second place was won by Chris Martin in the 200 with the good time of 22.2. Denzil Winsborrow had a busy afternoon with third in the high hurdles, an event in which he is rapidly improving, and in the high jump, and was also 4th in the pole vault.

Such names as Adrian Major, Bill Kerr, Chris Martin, 'Snowy' Brooks and Phillip Gee. These fellows were always prepared to turn up to any meeting in any conditions and without them Bels would certainly not have fared as well as they did.

Chris Martin, Cliff Brooks and the ubiquitous Tony Brooks have generally been on hand as able substitutes and Charles Gillet was "discovered" at Motspur Park, where he finished 2nd in the Surrey 200 metres (no-one knew he was first claim!).

The gale force wind ruled out good performances, as can be gauged by Chris Martin's winning 24.8 in the 220. Our only other winner was Brian King, who beat quite a fair field in the Javelin in very difficult throwing conditions.
Our best performances came from John Thresher and Geoff North in the 1500, Derek Glendinning and Bob Couillault in the Triple Jump and our "B" string sprinters Steve White and Chris Martin.

The senior sprints were annexed again by Chris Martin, whose main rival proved to be the fast improving Chris Sapountzoglou. Another impressive performance came in the steeplechase where Peter Morris moved smoothly to a personal best ahead of Dick Piotrowski.
Colin Gillett and Chris Martin took silver and bronze in the 200 metres, both in 22.9, and Chris also finished third in the 100 metres (11.5).
Probably our strongest events on paper with Steve White, Jim Vivian, John Mitchell and Chris Martin and able assistance from Aris Sapountzoglou, Tony and Cliff Brooks.
4 x 100m · 1. Belgrave (S. White, C. Gillett, C. Martin, J. Vivian) · 43.8s

Our Civil Service 880 yards champion, HAROLD TITHERLEY, was killed in an air-raid near the White City, C.MARTIN was lost at sea, and ALAN JERMAN - a most promising runner - killed in a motor-cycle accident while serving in the R.A.F: ARTHUR ALLUM, our first cross-country international, died followin…
Mick Marshall, Philip Gee, Chris Martin and Lee Sullivan were third in the sprint relay, and it was particularly good to see Chris sporting a Belgrave vest again.
A junior Belgrave squad came close to this in 1965 at Hurlingham (42.8 by John Mitchell, Denis Gleeson, Chris Martin and Jim Vivian) when winning the A.A.A.

Twentynine years ago at Crystal Palace, and Jim Vivian, Chris Martin, Robert Nelson and Dave Mitchell pose for the camera of Ed. Lacey after placing 6th in the final of the A.A.A. 4 x 220yds relay Championship in 1:31.9.
